chapter: Label, collaborations and the working artist
title: What he calls himself: artist, advocate, foundation support
summary: Describes his multiple roles and direct-to-artist funding from Meet the Composer, Creative Capital and the Ford Foundation committee.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience

blocks.x: Wow. When people ask you what you do, if they don’t know you too well, what do you say?

Well I say I’m an artist. And an artist has multiple roles. I’m a composer, a pianist, artistic director of ensembles, I’m also a spokesperson, an educator, I do intellectual work, that is, the arts advocacy work. Recently I served on the Arts Advisory Committee for the Ford Foundation which is going to launch a national initiative to provide direct support to artists. And this is one of the changing trends that I’m seeing in foundations and national service organizations. Because I was a recipient of a three-year residency program of Meet the Composer. That’s a national service organization in New York which fosters the creation, performance, production and dissemination of new work by living American composers. So that’s their mission statement. And what they did is they provided direct support to me. Because traditionally they used to provide direct support to an arts organization. And there was always problems. So that was, to me, an expression of validation of the artist. And then there’s Creative Capital Foundation which has provided direct support in a very strategic way — you know one year, two year, three year — and they’re part of a process where they do not want to be recognized as a funder but a partner. They want to have ownership in the work, but not ownership in sort of a corporate, capitalistic way, but in really — I mean Creative Capital is run by people who are in the arts world. So sometimes there’s a knee jerk reaction from other artists who are kind of disconnected from them, they just think oh your arts project is going to be co- opted. So I mean as an artist I don’t think of myself as like a musician — or no, I think of © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

myself as a musician but I don’t think of myself as somebody who does gigs. I mean most of what I do is the music of Jon Jang or the music of Jon Jang with the music of David Murray or the music of Max Roach. So I mean Max Roach is one of the greatest artists of the twentieth century.
